column1: # The macOS renderer's frames, drawn by wgpu 29.0.3's Metal backend (the
# `wgpu-oracle` build's arm, the differential the first-party Metal arm was
# held to until GW.6; docs/AUDIT-third-party-2026-10-15.md) on this Mac's
# GPU, with the system's monospace face and Apple Color Emoji, on macOS
# 27.0.1 (26A434), before wgpu left the workspace (recorded on the
# devendor/gw6 branch, 2026-10-26). One block per architecture and adapter.
# The first 102 rows are the readbacks, presents and window layer; the
# video take, the EDR presents, the blit rows and the crown rows were added
# from wgpu the same day (devendor/gw6-rec): `edr/*` is wgpu's EDR present,
# which Metal's production present into an `Rgba16Float` drawable must
# equal, and `blit/*` and `crown/*` are wgpu's present blit and crown rows,
# which the Metal rows run standalone (`metal::blit`) must equal. Every row
# was drawn by wgpu; a stated re-record names the rows it redrew and their
# drawer here. src/frame_record_tests.rs compares these rows as a signal on
# the adapter they name (its `frame-record` lines are these rows, and
# `frame-record: moved:` names a frame drawn otherwise); since
# ORACLE-ADAPTER (2026-10-26) the verdict is each frame's CPU twin, decided
# on any adapter, and a moved row fails nothing. Columns: arch, adapter, frame, WxH, SHA-256 of the bytes
# (RGBA8 for a readback, present, layer or take; the destination's texels
